extracted.intended_audience: Users of SINGULAR (computational algebra/geometry researchers) who use resolve.lib and reszeta.lib for desingularization and related computations
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for SINGULAR library procedures (resolve.lib and reszeta.lib) used for resolution of singularities, blowing up, computing centers, Delta-operators, and computing topological/spectral invariants. Each entry specifies usage, assumptions, what is computed, return values, and examples/notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: blowUp2
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: blowUp2(J,C); J,C = ideals. Assume: C = ideal containing J. Note: C is the ideal of the center of the blowup and J the ideal of the variety. Important differences to blowUp: V(J) itself is blown up, not the ambient space; C is not assumed to be non-singular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute: the blowing up of J in C, the exceptional locus and the blow-up map. Return: list l of size at most size(C); l[i] is the affine ring corresponding to the i-th chart. Each l[i] contains the ideals: Jnew (ideal of the blownup J), eD (ideal of the new exceptional divisor), bM (ideal corresponding to the blowup map). Example: demonstrates calling LIB "resolve.lib"; ring setup; li=blowUp2(I,C); then inspecting li[1]/li[2] for Jnew, eD, bM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Center
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: Center(J[,W][,E]) where J,W = ideals and E = list. Assume: J = ideal containing W (W = 0 if not specified); E = list of smooth hypersurfaces (e.g. exceptional divisors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute: the center of the blow-up of J for the resolution algorithm of [Bravo,Encinas,Villamayor]. Return: ideal describing the center. Example: LIB "resolve.lib"; ring R=0,(x,y),dp; ideal J=x2-y3; Center(J); → outputs an ideal (example shows y,x).

rubrics_metrics.name: resolve
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: resolve(J); or resolve(J,i[,k]); J ideal; i,k integers. Compute: a resolution of J.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Debugging: if i>0 debugging is turned on according to switches j1..j6 (j1 correctness checks; j2 debugCenter; j3 debugBlowUp; j4 debugCoeff; j5 debugging of Intersection with E^-; j6 stop after pass through loop). i = j1+j2+...+j6. Return: a list L of 2 lists of rings: L[1][i] is a ring containing a basic object BO, the result of the resolution; L[2] contains all rings which occurred during the resolution process. Note: result may be viewed in human-readable form using presentTree(). Example: shows resolve(J,0) and inspecting a BO with showBO.

rubrics_metrics.name: showBO
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: showBO(BO); BO = basic object, a list: ideal W, ideal J, intvec b (truncated for Coeff), list Ex (truncated for Coeff), ideal ab, intvec v, intvec w (truncated for Coeff), matrix M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: nothing — only pretty printing. Purpose: human-readable display of Ambient Space, Ideal of Variety, Exceptional Divisors, Images of variables, etc. Example: used after resolve to display BO content.

rubrics_metrics.name: presentTree
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: presentTree(L); L = list, output of resolve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: nothing — pretty printing of the output data of resolve(). Use to view the chart/tree structure of the resolution in a readable form.

rubrics_metrics.name: showDataTypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: showDataTypes();
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: nothing — pretty printing of extended version of help text. Purpose: show data type definitions and extended help for resolve.lib.

rubrics_metrics.name: blowUpBO
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: blowUpBO(BO,C,e); BO = basic object (list: ideal W, ideal J, intvec b, list Ex, ideal ab, intvec v, intvec w, matrix M); C = ideal; e = integer (0 usual blowing up, 1 deleting extra charts, 2 deleting no charts). Assume: basering R a polynomial ring, W an ideal of R, J = ideal containing W, C = ideal containing J.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute: the blowing up of BO[1] in C, the exceptional locus, the strict transform of BO[2]. Note: blowUpBO may be applied to 'basic objects' (BO) in the sense of [Bravo,Encinas,Villamayor] and to 'presentations' in the sense of [Bierstone,Milman] (BM). Return: a list l of length at most size(C), where each l[i] is a ring containing an object BO or BM with components: BO[1]=Wi defining ambient space of i-th chart; BO[2] strict transform ideal; BO[3] intvec (first integer b s.t. (Delta^b(BO[2]))==1); BM[3] assigned multiplicities; BO[4] list of exceptional divisors; BO[5] ideal defining the map K[W] -> K[Wi]; BO[6] intvec indicator of strict transform not meeting j-th exceptional divisor; BO[7] intvec index info for resolution history; BO[8] matrix indicating intersections of exceptional divisors; BO[9] empty; BM[9] the invariant. Example: shows constructing BO and calling blowUpBO, then inspecting returned BO components.

rubrics_metrics.name: createBO
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: createBO(J[,W][,E]); J,W = ideals; E = list. Assume: J = ideal containing W (W = 0 if not specified); E = list of smooth hypersurfaces (e.g. exceptional divisors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: list BO representing a basic object with entries: BO[1] ideal W if specified else ideal(0); BO[2] ideal J; BO[3] intvec; BO[4] list E if specified else empty; BO[5] ideal defining identity map; BO[6] intvec; BO[7] intvec; BO[8] matrix. Entries 3,5,6,7,8 initialized appropriately for use of CenterBO and blowUpBO. Example: createBO(J,ideal(z)) and printed structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: CenterBO
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: CenterBO(BO); BO = basic object (list: ideal W, ideal J, intvec b, list Ex, ideal ab, intvec v, intvec w, matrix M). Assume: basering R a polynomial ring, W an ideal of R, J = ideal containing W.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute: the center (in the sense of [Bravo,Encinas,Villamayor]) of the next blow-up of BO in the resolution algorithm. Return: list l with l[1] = ideal describing the center; l[2] = intvec w obtained during determination; l[3] = intvec b obtained; l[4] = intvec inv obtained. Example: constructs BO and calls CenterBO, showing outputs (center ideal and intvecs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Delta
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: Delta(BO); BO = basic object (list: ideal W, ideal J, intvec b, list Ex, ideal ab, intvec v, intvec w, matrix M). Assume: basering R a polynomial ring, W an ideal of R, J = ideal containing W.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute: Delta-operator applied to J in the notation of [Bravo,Encinas,Villamayor]. Return: ideal (the result of applying Delta). Example: shows Delta(BO) producing a list of polynomials representing Delta(J).

rubrics_metrics.name: DeltaList
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: DeltaList(BO); BO = basic object. Assume: basering R a polynomial ring, W an ideal of R, J = ideal containing W.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute: Delta-operator iteratively applied to J in the notation of [Bravo,Encinas,Villamayor]. Return: list l of length ((max w-ord) * b), where l[i+1] = Delta^i(J). Example: demonstrates DeltaList(BO) returning successive Delta powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: reszeta.lib (library purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Library: reszeta.lib. Purpose: topological Zeta-function and some other applications of desingularization. Authors and references listed (Fruehbis-Krueger, Pfister, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides procedures that operate on the output of resolve() (list of rings) to compute intersection matrices, genera, spectral numbers, discrepancies, Denef–Loeser zeta functions and helper routines for identifying exceptional divisors and embedded components. See the following procedure-level entries for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: intersectionDiv
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: intersectionDiv(L); L = list of rings. Assume: L is output of resolution of singularities (only case of isolated surface singularities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute: intersection matrix and genera of the exceptional divisors (considered as curves on the strict transform). Return: list l where l[1] is intersection matrix of exceptional divisors; l[2] intvec of genera of exceptional divisors; l[3] divisorList encoding identification of the divisors. Example: shows calling resolve(J) then intersectionDiv(re) and printing matrix and genera.

rubrics_metrics.name: spectralNeg
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: spectralNeg(L); L = list of rings. Assume: L is output of resolution of singularities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: list of numbers, each a spectral number in (-1,0]. Example: calling spectralNeg(L) on a resolved singularity yields spectral numbers such as -13/60, -1/60; example also shows usage of gmssing.lib spectrum(f) to produce full spectrum.

rubrics_metrics.name: discrepancy
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: discrepancy(L); L = list of rings. Assume: L is the output of resolution of singularities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: discrepancies of the given resolution (example: discrepancy(re) → 0,1,1). Purpose: compute discrepancy values for each exceptional divisor in the resolution data.

rubrics_metrics.name: zetaDL
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: zetaDL(L,...) where L = output of resolve. Assume: L is the output of resolution of singularities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute/Return: the local Denef–Loeser zeta function if string s1='local', otherwise the global Denef–Loeser zeta function. If string s1 or s2 has value 'A', additionally compute the characteristic polynomial of the monodromy. Returned list l contents vary depending on presence of 'a': if 'a' not present: l[1] string specifying topological zeta function; l[2] string specifying characteristic polynomial of monodromy if 'A' specified. If 'a' present: l[1] string specifying topological zeta; l[2] list ast with ast[1]=chi(Ei^*), ast[2]=chi(Eij^*), ast[3]=chi(Eijk^*); l[3] intvec nu of multiplicities; l[4] intvec N of multiplicities; l[5] string for characteristic polynomial if 'A' specified. Examples: shows zetaDL(re,1) and printouts (rational function expressions and expected forms).

rubrics_metrics.name: collectDiv
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: collectDiv(L); L = list of rings. Assume: L is output of resolution of singularities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute: list representing the identification of the exceptional divisors in the various charts. Return: list where l[1] is an intmat encoding which BO[4][j] of chart i is divisor k (k!=0); l[2] list ll where each ll[k] is list of intvecs identifying positions of divisor k across charts; l[3] list L. Example: demonstrates calling collectDiv on resolve(I) and shows returned matrices and lists mapping divisors across charts.

rubrics_metrics.name: prepEmbDiv
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: prepEmbDiv(L[,a]); L = list of rings; a = integer optional. Assume: L is output of resolution of singularities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute: if a not present: exceptional divisors including components of the strict transform; otherwise: only exceptional divisors. Return: list of Q-irreducible exceptional divisors (embedded case). Example: prepEmbDiv(L) on a resolved ideal returns lists labeling divisors with multiplicities and chart/embedding data.

rubrics_metrics.name: abstractR
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: abstractR(L); L = list of rings. Assume: L is output of resolve. Note: currently only implemented for isolated surface singularities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: list l where l[1] is an intvec with l[1][i]=1 if corresponding ring is a final chart of non-embedded resolution (0 otherwise); l[2] intvec with l[2][i]=1 if the corresponding ring does not occur in the non-embedded resolution (0 otherwise); l[3] list L. Example: abstractR(L) returns indicator vectors identifying final charts and charts not used in non-embedded resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: computeV
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: computeV(L,DL); L = list of rings (output of resolve); DL = divisor list (output of prepEmbDiv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute/Return: intvec where the i-th entry is the multiplicity of the i-th divisor in the pullback of the volume form. Example: demonstrates using resolve(I,1) then inspecting chart-overviews and calling computeV to get multiplicities for divisors.
